title: Talpur Dynasty
capsule: The Talpur dynasty was a Baloch Shia ruling house that came to power in Sindh in 1783 when Mir Fateh Ali Khan Talpur defeated the Kalhora ruler at the Battle of Halani and established his capital at Hyderabad. The dynasty governed Sindh through a distributed system among three branches — the Mirs of Hyderabad, Khairpur, and Mirpur Khas — which diffused authority and impeded coordinated resistance to external threats. British East India Company forces under General Charles Napier defeated the Hyderabad Talpurs at the Battle of Miani on 17 February 1843 and annexed Sindh; the Khairpur branch survived as a princely state under British paramountcy until accession to Pakistan in 1955, and the dataset terminus of 1895 likely reflects a specific administrative reorganization within that subordinate arrangement.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core Talpur territory in Sindh is reasonably well documented from British East India Company records and Sindhi chronicles; the significance of the 1895 terminus in the dataset is unclear and may reflect the Khairpur branch's partial continuation.
